visibleFaq.question: What does mainstream participation mean?
visibleFaq.answer: It means meaningful participation in ordinary family, school, play and community life with appropriate support and access. Goals, settings and support differ for each child.

visibleFaq.question: Is mainstream inclusion the same as school admission?
visibleFaq.answer: No. Admission is one event. Participation also involves learning access, communicating needs, relationships, comfort and suitable support. A school and family make placement decisions using relevant professional advice and the child’s circumstances.

visibleFaq.question: How do the seven Readiness Indexes help?
visibleFaq.answer: Pinnacle’s separate readiness views support conversations about developmental priorities, including school, self-sufficiency and mainstream participation. They are read with abilities, context and professional judgement; they are not an automatic placement decision.

visibleFaq.question: Can the family and school work together?
visibleFaq.answer: Yes. Relevant family observations and, with your consent, teacher observations can help guide meaningful priorities and review. Ask how information will be shared and who will use it.

visibleFaq.question: Does Pinnacle guarantee mainstream admission or an outcome?
visibleFaq.answer: No. The programme works toward meaningful participation with child-specific support. The software’s regulatory scope and research records do not guarantee admission, independence or an individual outcome.

visibleFaq.question: How can we start?
visibleFaq.answer: Call 9100 181 181 with one part of school, play or community life you want to make more possible. The team can help confirm a suitable professional, centre, service, appointment and fee before a visit.
